land.text: the western half of the Kushan realm: Bactria, Sogdia and the Kabul valley

predecessors.note: Kushan Empire page: 'After the death of Vasudeva I in 225, the Kushan empire split into western and eastern halves'; the western half was 'soon subjugated by the Persian Sasanian Empire'. Cliopatria starts the half in 238; the page's year is 225, so it starts here in 226.

land.text: Bactria, Sogdia, Kabul and Gandhara: the Kushano-Sasanian Kingdom, 'established c. 230' and ended c. 365 on its page; every one of the 2,351 cells of the Western Kushans' shape lies inside Cliopatria's Indo-Sasanian shape of 260

successors.note: The two Cliopatria rows are the same Kushanshah-ruled kingdom: Western Kushans (238-259) and Indo-Sasanian Empire (260-357, Wikipedia title Kushano-Sasanian Kingdom, Wikidata Q1661685). The kingdom is the continuation, not a conquest in 260; the colour agent should treat the two rows as one line.

capitals.name: Balkh (Bactra)
capitals.note: Infobox of the Kushano-Sasanian Kingdom page: Capital: Balkh. The pages opened give no capital for the Western Kushans before the Sasanian governors.

rulers.name: Ardashir I Kushanshah
rulers.note: The page's list gives 230-245; its infobox gives 233-245. A Sasanian governor, not a Kushan king: 'The local Sasanian governors then went on to take the title of Kushanshah'.

rulers.name: Peroz I Kushanshah
rulers.note: The page's list: 245-275; Hormizd I follows 275-300. Reviewer (sa-02-c): clipped to the dossier's end, 259; the reign continues in indo-sasanian-empire.

correction.text: the 238 shape held 12 years earlier: Bactria, Sogdia and the Kabul valley

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria starts the Western Kushans in 238; the Kushan Empire page puts the division of the empire just after the death of Vasudeva I in 225, and the Kushano-Sasanian page has the Sasanians capturing Sogdia, Bactria and Gandhara in 225 and extending their dominion into Bactria around 230. The Kushan Empire row (to 237) is, to within 54 cells, the union of the two halves' 238 shapes, so the western half is drawn from 226 with the 238 outline. The pages give no area for the division (the infobox's 2.0-2.5 M km2 for c. 200 is for the undivided empire; this half is 0.68 M km2 and the eastern one 1.24 M).

0.68 M km2 for 238-246: Bactria (30% of the shape), Sogdia, the Kabul valley, Arachosia (45% of the region) and the Fergana edge, 32% of Gandhara. The Kushano-Sasanian page has the Sasanians holding 'Sogdia, Bactria and Gandhara' and says the kingdom's farthest eastern extent 'appears to have been Gandhara', with mints at Kabul, Balkh, Herat and Merv; the shape holds Kabul and Balkh but not Herat or Merv (Cliopatria's Sasanian shape) and gives most of Gandhara to the Eastern Kushans. The land is Sasanian-ruled through Kushanshah governors from about 230, so the state is a vassal kingdom, not an independent Kushan state.
Identical to 238 (684,686 km2); Peroz I Kushanshah (245-275) is on the throne. The page dates nothing in 247.

region.text: Bactria, Sogdia and the Kabul valley

ledger.note: 226: the western half of the Kushan realm divides from the east. 'After the death of Vasudeva I in 225, the Kushan empire split into western and eastern halves'; the western half was 'soon subjugated by the Persian Sasanian Empire and lost Sogdiana, Bactria, and Gandhara to them'. The Vasudeva I dates differ on the page (died 225; list c. 190-230). Cliopatria begins the half in 238.

c. 230: Sasanian governors take over as Kushanshahs. 'The Sasanian Empire captured the provinces of Sogdia, Bactria and Gandhara from the declining Kushan Empire' in 225 and 'extended their dominion into Bactria during the reign of Ardashir I around 230'; 'the local Sasanian governors then went on to take the title of Kushanshah' (Ardashir I 230-245). The Kushan Empire page: the Sasanians 'deposed the Western dynasty and replaced them with Persian vassals known as the Kushanshas'. Same state, same land, new dynasty and suzerain: this dossier now records the vassal relation (vassal_start 230, counterpart sasanian-empire); the Sasanian dossier should record the mirror (vassal_start, counterpart western-kushans).

region.text: the whole Kushanshah kingdom: Bactria, Sogdia and the Kabul valley

ledger.note: c. 230: the Kushanshah kingdom is a Sasanian dependency. Kushano-Sasanian Kingdom page (re-read 2026-10-19): 'The Sasanian Empire captured the provinces of Sogdia, Bactria and Gandhara from the declining Kushan Empire' (following a series of wars in 225 CE); 'The Sassanids ... extended their dominion into Bactria during the reign of Ardashir I around 230 CE'; 'The local Sasanian governors then went on to take the title of Kushanshah'; and they 'are sometimes considered as forming a "sub-kingdom" inside the Sasanian Empire'. The page does not use the word vassal; the relation is the reading of governors under Ardashir I (Ardashir I Kushanshah 230-245), and the Kushan Empire page says the Sasanians 'replaced them with Persian vassals known as the Kushanshas'. 230 is the page's year for Ardashir I's dominion; the capture in 225 precedes this dossier's start (226) and whether the western half was independent between 225 and 230 is page-silent. No vassal_end: the relation lasts to the end of this dossier (259) and continues in indo-sasanian-empire (the same kingdom, Wikidata Q1661685 with sasanian-empire), where me-06 should carry it. Added by the reviewer's finding (sa-02-c).

259: the Kushanshah kingdom continues as the Kushano-Sasanian (Indo-Sasanian) Kingdom. The page dates the kingdom c. 230 to c. 365 with Peroz I (245-275) and Hormizd I (275-300) as its Kushanshahs, so nothing ends in 259; Cliopatria changes the row name in 260 and the whole 247 shape (2,351 cells) lies in the Indo-Sasanian shape of 260.

wars.name: Sasanian conquest of the Kushan lands

zones.text: Sogdia and Bactria, taken in 225 and 'around 230' under Ardashir I

wars.outcome: The Sasanians captured Sogdia, Bactria and Gandhara, installed Kushanshah governors and extended to western Pakistan under Shapur I (240-270).
wars.note: One process with three dates on the page: 225 (capture), about 230 (Ardashir I in Bactria), 240-270 (Shapur I in the east).

certainty.note: The Bactrian, Kabul and Gandharan limits are inferred from mints and inscriptions, not from lines; the Sasanian frontier with the Eastern Kushans at the Indus is approximate.

sources.title: Kushan Empire

sources.title: Kushano-Sasanian Kingdom
sources.note: Sasanian capture (225, c. 230, 240-270), Kushanshah list (Ardashir I 230-245, Peroz I 245-275), Balkh capital, mints, c. 230-c. 365.

notes:
Pages opened: two of the 1-2 page budget (Kushan Empire, Kushano-Sasanian Kingdom).

A state or a label: Cliopatria's Western Kushans (238-259) are, on the pages, the Kushan Empire's western half under Sasanian governors titled Kushanshah from about 230, i.e. the early Kushano-Sasanian Kingdom. Every one of the 2,351 cells of the 238-259 shape lies inside Cliopatria's Indo-Sasanian Empire shape of 260, and that row's Wikipedia title is Kushano-Sasanian Kingdom (Q1661685, a Wikidata id it shares with the Sasanian Empire row). So this dossier is a short-lived Kushan successor that became a Sasanian vassal kingdom; the me-06 group's indo-sasanian-empire dossier should be read with it, and one of the two should hold the kingdom's whole life (c. 230-c. 365) with the other cross-referencing it. Other dossiers (kidarites) use the slug kushano-sasanian-kingdom, which has no dossier; it should resolve to indo-sasanian-empire.

Family: persia, not india: the pages say the Sasanians 'deposed the Western dynasty and replaced them with Persian vassals'; Cliopatria's colour for this row should read as a lighter Sasanian tint rather than a Kushan colour.

Unsettled: (a) the Western Kushans' independence between 225 and about 230 is page-silent; (b) Gandhara is mostly outside the shape (Eastern Kushans to 259) although the pages give it to the Sasanians by 225 or 240-270; (c) Herat and Merv, Kushano-Sasanian mints per the page, are Cliopatria Sasanian land; (d) the foundation of the Kushanshah governorship is dated 225, c. 230 and 233 on the same pages.

Counterparts needing dossiers: none beyond indo-sasanian-empire and sasanian-empire (me-06), which should record the vassal relation.

Repair (sa-02-c-fixed, 2026-10-19): the Sasanian overlordship is now in this dossier as a vassal_start at 230 (counterpart sasanian-empire, Kushano-Sasanian Kingdom page, confidence 2) next to the rename; the page says 'around 230' for Ardashir I's dominion in Bactria and 225 for the capture, and 'sub-kingdom' for the Kushanshahs, never vassal. There is no vassal_end because the relation runs to this dossier's end (259) and on into indo-sasanian-empire; the validator therefore prints one warning for the open vassal_start, which its own message calls fine in that case. The mirror (vassal_start, counterpart western-kushans, 230) belongs in the sasanian-empire dossier (me-06). The Kushano-Sasanian Kingdom page runs the kingdom c. 230 to c. 365, so the 259 end is Cliopatria's row change, as noted above.
